lessonRef.title: Reteach and varied practice: payroll income sales property and excise tax concepts
lessonRef.focus: payroll income sales property and excise tax concepts

objective: Learners re-practise computing invented sales, excise, and property taxes on their different bases.
scenario: Quintus is an invented eighth grader computing three pretend taxes: 6.25% sales tax on a $320.00 purchase, an invented excise charge of $0.18 per unit on 400 units, and 1.2% property tax on an invented $150,000.00 valuation. All figures are invented.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Compute the invented sales tax on Quintus's $320.00 purchase at 6.25%.

prompts.text: How much sales tax is charged?

tasks.directions: Compute Quintus's invented excise charge on 400 units and the property tax on the stated valuation.

prompts.text: What does the excise charge come to on 400 units?
What does the 1.2% property tax come to?

tasks.directions: Total Quintus's three taxes and express the property tax on a monthly basis.

prompts.text: What do all three taxes come to?
What is the monthly share of the property tax?

tasks.directions: One tax was charged per unit rather than per dollar.

prompts.text: Explain how Quintus's excise charge differs from a percentage tax, and what happens to its real burden when prices rise.

remediation: If a learner applies a percentage to the unit count, label each of Quintus's taxes with its base before any computation.
extension: Ask the learner what excise rate per unit would raise the same amount as the sales tax on Quintus's purchase.
